notes: Python, JavaScript and TypeScript rebuilt from beginner to professional, each with a new "Working like a pro" unit: project setup, linting, testing, CI, web servers, packaging and more
JavaScript: 18 new lessons, including debugging, metaprogramming, streams, workers, security pitfalls and WebAssembly; every lesson now uses ES modules
TypeScript: 14 new lessons, including reading type errors, decorators, variance, declaration files, typed routers and React-style reducers; targets TypeScript 6 and 7
Every exercise in these courses has tests proven to reject common wrong answers, every lesson has a "Common mistakes" note, and capstone projects show milestones as you go
Each course page now says which language version it teaches
Fixes: C# and Clojure programs now run (they download what they need once, then work offline), outdated examples in Zig, Ruby, PHP and F#, and beginner hints that weren't true in every language
